title.narrative: ADRA - Somalia WASH Delivery Improvement Program

description.narrative:
Project objectives: Improved health and environmental conditions by sustained access to WASH services contributing to reduced poverty and improved economic status of Somali people.
Outcome 1: Strengthened enabling environment and governance structure supporting delivery of appropriate, equitable and affordable WASH services. Outcome 2: Increased access to sustained, reliable, equitable and affordable safe water through well managed water supply systems in rural, peri-urban areas and urban centres. Outcome 3: Increased access to improved, adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene services in rural, peri-urban and urban areas.
The following two objectives were removed for the extension period 2024-2025: Outcome 4: Improved economic performance of local livelihoods reliant on improved access to WASH services Outcome 5: An enabling environment for the efficient and effective delivery of humanitarian and development assistance for all Somali people.

Organisationen The Adventist Development Relief Agency (ADRA) har ansökt till Sida om finansiering på 68 miljoner kronor för att genomföra programmet Somalia WASH Service Delivery Improvement Program (SOWASDIP)" i Somalia under perioden 2019-2023. Detta inkluderar 8 000 000 kronor som Sida har tilldelat för att stödja arbetet i Somalia NGO Consortium under samma period.
Programmet syftar till att förbättra hälso- och miljöförhållandena för en fortsatt tillgång till vatten-, sanitets- och hygienbaserade tjänster (WASH). Specifikt kommer programmet att: 1) Stärka de möjliggörande faktorerna och governance-strukturerna för att stödja leverans av lämpliga, rättvisa och prisvärda WASH-tjänster, 2) öka tillgången till hållbart, rättvist och billigt säkert vatten genom välskötta vattenförsörjningssystem på landsbygden, i städer och i utkanter av städer 3) öka tillgången till förbättrade, lämpliga och rättvisa sanitets- och hygientjänster, och 4) Ökad hushållsinkomst som ett resultat förbättrade WASH-tjänster. ADRA kommer att genomföra programmet tillsammans med den somaliska regeringen, det civila samhällets organisationer, den privata sektorn och det somaliska NGO-konsortiet. Programmet kommer geografiskt att riktas sig till utvalda distrikt i South Central, Puntland, Somaliland och staterna Galmudug, South West och Jubbaland. Primära målgrupper kommer att vara kvinnor och flickor från fattiga hushåll som bor i städer, i utkanten av städer och på landsbygden, inklusive de nomadiska befolkningarna och internflyktingar.
Programmets totala budget uppgår till 68 miljoner kronor med Sida som enda finansiär. Cirka 15 miljoner kronor av programbudgeten kommer att vidarebefordras från ADRA till genomförande av civila samhällsorganisationer och 8 miljoner kronor till NGO-konsortiet.

The Adventist Development Relief Agency (ADRA) has applied to Sida for funding of 68 million SEK to carry out the 'Somalia WASH Service Delivery Improvement Programme (SOWASDIP)' in Somalia during the period 2019-2023. This includes SEK 8 000 000 that Sida has allocated to support the work of the Somalia NGO Consortium during the same period.
The intervention aims at improving health and environmental conditions as a result of sustained access to water, sanitation and hygiene promotion (WASH) services. Specifically, the intervention will 1) Strengthen the enabling environment and governance structures to support the delivery of appropriate, equitable and affordable WASH services, 2) increase access to sustained, equitable and affordable safe water through well managed water supply systems in rural, peri-urban and urban settlements, 3) increase access to improved, adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene services, and 4) Increased household income as a result improved WASH services . ADRA will implement the intervention together with the Somali governments, Civil Society Organizations, the private sector, and the Somalia NGO consortium. The intervention will geographically target select districts in South Central, Puntland, Somaliland and the states (Galmudug, South West, and Jubbaland). Primary target beneficiaries will be women and girls from poor households living in urban, peri-urban and rural areas including the nomadic populations and Internally Displaced Persons.
The intervention’s total budget is 68 million SEK which will be totally funded by Sida. Approximately 17 million SEK of the intervention budget will be forwarded from ADRA to implementing civil society organizations and 8 MSEK to the NGO consortium.

description.narrative:
Key Achievements 2019-2025
- Directly benefited 383,757 people (196,593 women and girls; 191,164 men and boys) across Somalia through improved WASH services. - Reached more than 4.5 million people indirectly through hygiene promotion and mass media awareness campaigns. - Implemented across Jubaland, Galmudug, Puntland, Southwest State, Hirshabelle, Somaliland, and Banadir
Strengthened WASH Governance and Capacity (Result 1) - 2,450 people reached through capacity-building and community participation activities, achieving 130% of the target. - Supported 3 Federal Member States to develop and adopt WASH policies. - Trained 141 water management committee members to strengthen local governance and sustainability of water systems. - Trained 75 water operators in operation and maintenance of water infrastructure. - Supported government-led WASH sector coordination through steering committee meetings, monitoring missions, learning events, and infrastructure commissioning initiatives.
Increased Access to Safe Water (Result 2) - 193,933 people gained access to improved and reliable water supplies. - Established, rehabilitated or upgraded 33 water supply systems across programme locations. - Rehabilitated and expanded 28 strategic water supply systems, greatly exceeding programme targets. - Constructed or rehabilitated 5 lined earth dams (hafir dams) to improve water storage and drought resilience. - Installed 24.2 km of water distribution pipelines, extending water services to communities, schools, and health facilities. - Improved access to water for vulnerable rural and peri-urban populations while supporting livestock and livelihood activities.
Improved Sanitation and Hygiene (Result 3) - 118,922 people reached directly through sanitation and hygiene interventions. - 147,348 people gained improved access to sanitation facilities and services. - Implemented Community-Led Total Sanitation (CLTS) in 47 communities. - Facilitated the construction of 2,937 household latrines, benefiting more than 17,600 people. - Achieved 81% Open Defecation Free (ODF) certification, surpassing the target of 80%, with 38 communities certified ODF. - Conducted environmental sanitation campaigns reaching 13,076 people.
Water, Sanitation and Hygiene in Schools (WinS) - Implemented WinS programming in 58 schools, benefiting 28,610 learners. - Improved sanitation facilities and hygiene infrastructure for nearly 20,000 students. - Extended water access to 6,758 learners through school water connections. - Trained 173 teachers and school committee representatives on WinS approaches. - Distributed dignity kits to 7,279 adolescent girls to support menstrual hygiene management. - Established 13 girl-friendly spaces in schools, creating safer and more inclusive learning environments.
Hygiene Promotion and Behaviour Change -Reached 181,708 people through community hygiene awareness and behaviour change campaigns. -Reached over 4.5 million people through radio campaigns and mass media messaging, dramatically exceeding programme targets. - Supported 66 global and national WASH awareness events, promoting improved hygiene practices and public engagement.
Improved Urban Health and Municipal Sanitation (Result 4) - 109,937 people benefited from urban sanitation and public health improvements. - Established 3 municipal waste disposal sites in Qardho, Sheikh, and Dhobley. - Rehabilitated 2 public abattoirs and improved faecal sludge and wastewater management systems. - Strengthened municipal capacity to manage solid waste and improve environmental health in urban centres.
Overall Impact - Demonstrated the effectiveness of community-driven, government-led, and market-based WASH approaches in fragile contexts. - Strengthened institutions and community structures for sustainable service delivery. - Improved access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for hundreds of thousands of Somalis. - Contributed to healthier communities, reduced open defecation, improved hygiene practices, and strengthened resilience to climate and public health challenges.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
